Create object HotspotChoice

Source: R/HotspotChoice.R
hotspotChoice.Rd

Create object HotspotChoice

Usage

hotspotChoice(
  identifier = generate_id(),
  title = identifier,
  image,
  image_width,
  image_height,
  shapes,
  coords,
  choices = paste("Hotspot", seq_along(shapes)),
  choice_identifiers = paste0("Hotspot", seq_along(shapes)),
  content = list(),
  prompt = "",
  points = 1,
  feedback = list(),
  image_alt = "Abbildung",
  max_choices = 0,
  calculator = NA_character_,
  files = NA_character_,
  scoring_scheme = "standard",
  response_identifier = "RESPONSE",
  template = list()
)

Arguments

identifier

A character representing the unique identifier of the assessment task. By default, it is generated as 'id_task_dddd', where dddd represents random digits.

title

A character representing the title of the XML file associated with the task. By default, it takes the value of the identifier.

image

A character, path to the image (PNG, JPEG, GIF or SVG) or a data URI.

image_width, image_height

Numeric, size of the image in pixels; the coordinates refer to this size.

shapes

A character vector, the shape of each hotspot: "circle", "rect", "poly" or "ellipse".

coords

A character vector, the coordinates of each hotspot in pixels, see HotspotChoice.

choices

A character vector, a label for each hotspot. The labels are not shown to candidates; they document the hotspots, e.g. for results.

choice_identifiers

A character vector, optional, containing a set of identifiers for answers. By default, identifiers are generated automatically according to the template "ChoiceD", where D is a letter representing the alphabetical order of the answer in the list.

content

A character string or a list of character strings to form the text of the question, which may include HTML tags.

prompt

An optional character representing a simple question text, consisting of one paragraph. This can supplement or replace content in the task. Default is "".

points

A numeric vector, required. Each number in this vector determines the number of points that will be awarded to a candidate if they select the corresponding answer. The order of the scores must match the order of the choices. It is possible to assign negative values to incorrect answers. All answers with a positive score are considered correct.

feedback

A list containing feedback messages for candidates. Each element of the list should be an instance of either ModalFeedback, CorrectFeedback, or WrongFeedback class.

image_alt

A character, text alternative of the image.

max_choices

A numeric, the maximum number of hotspots to select; 0 (default) means no limit, 1 a single hotspot.

calculator

A character, optional, determining whether to show a calculator to the candidate. Possible values:

  • "simple"

  • "scientific".

files

A character vector, optional, containing paths to files that will be accessible to the candidate during the test/exam.

scoring_scheme

A method name or specification from multiple_choice_scoring(). The default "standard" retains the existing balanced mapping and zero floor.

response_identifier

QTI response identifier. Default "RESPONSE". Must be a valid identifier distinct from the item's score and feedback outcome identifiers.

template

A list of MaximaVariables objects, for example created with maxima_variables(). Defaults to an empty list. Blocks run in list order when the exported item is delivered by a player supporting MAXIMA.

Value

An object of class HotspotChoice

Examples

img <- tempfile(fileext = ".png")
grDevices::png(img, width = 300, height = 200)
graphics::par(mar = c(0, 0, 0, 0))
graphics::plot.new()
graphics::rect(0.05, 0.1, 0.45, 0.9)
graphics::rect(0.55, 0.1, 0.95, 0.9)
grDevices::dev.off()
#> agg_record_1979533f6bba 
#>                       2 
hotspotChoice(image = img, image_width = 300, image_height = 200,
              shapes = c("rect", "rect"),
              coords = c("15,20,135,180", "165,20,285,180"),
              choices = c("left", "right"), points = c(1, 0),
              content = "<p>Click on the left rectangle.</p>")
